notes: Signs identified visually from Budge's type. Recurring uncertain identifications: the upright tall rectangle with a side tie is coded Y1 (papyrus roll set vertically); the dashed upright of three short strokes is coded Z3; the beaker-shaped sign in śeta is coded W24; the bumped horizontal 'àn' negation sign is coded D35; the fringed bar on two uprights (cloth determinative) is coded S28; a low flat sign with an upturned squared right end and hooked left end (in seχem, ḥebs-nà, ḥau, χer-sek, θesu) is coded D36 though it may be a different sign; the tall spike on a small base (t'at'at, t'a-kuà) is coded U28; the tall tapered upright with tie and bell foot (sensen-à, sentrà) is coded T22. Where a papyrus-line numeral falls inside a word, the word is assigned to the line in which it begins (noted in 'unsure'). Rubric overlines seen on p.189 line 1 (Re en āq er; ṭua), p.189 (t'eṭ àn), p.192 (t'eṭ àn), p.193 (t'eṭ an). Capital À used for Budge's accented capital A (Àusàr, Àmentet, Ànpu, Àbṭu).
